package_info.why_malicious: These versions of struts2-core contain a critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability in the HttpParameters class. Attackers can exploit improper case-insensitive handling of HTTP parameter names to bypass security checks, allowing arbitrary code execution on affected servers. This makes the affected versions highly dangerous if not patched.

execution_context.trigger: During HTTP request processing at runtime

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During HTTP request processing at runtime, the code uses equalsIgnoreCase to compare HTTP parameter names, allowing attackers to submit parameters with varied casing that bypass security checks, resulting in attacker-controlled input being processed and leading to remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of equalsIgnoreCase in a security-sensitive context allows attackers to bypass intended access controls by manipulating the casing of HTTP parameter names, enabling injection of malicious payloads.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior expects strict, case-sensitive validation and sanitization of HTTP parameters, especially before using them in code execution paths. The actual behavior allows case-insensitive matching, which attackers exploit to bypass security logic and achieve code execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Case-insensitive parameter handling may be used for user convenience in non-security-critical contexts, but should never be used where parameter names control access or execution logic.
key_indicators: equalsIgnoreCase used for HTTP parameter name comparison in security logic
User-supplied input flows into code execution paths without strict validation
Absence of input sanitization or canonicalization before processing parameters

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a specially crafted HTTP request with parameter names using mixed or unusual casing to exploit case-insensitive comparison.
attack_chain.leads_to: Bypass of security checks in HTTP parameter processing.

attack_chain.action: The vulnerable code processes the malicious input, allowing attacker-controlled data to reach code execution paths.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution on the server, enabling full compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Inbound HTTP requests to .action endpoints with mixed-case or unusual parameter names
Unexpected process execution (e.g., spawning of shell or system processes) triggered by web requests
Abnormal file writes or modifications on the server immediately following HTTP requests with suspicious parameters
file_indicators: Any custom or third-party artifact containing a copy or subclass of the vulnerable HttpParameters class
network_indicators: Inbound HTTP requests to .action endpoints with parameter names differing only in case from expected values
Outbound network connections initiated by the web application process following such HTTP requests
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor HTTP traffic for requests to .action endpoints with mixed-case or unexpected parameter names. Analyze application logs for errors, stack traces, or unusual activity involving HttpParameters. Use static code analysis to identify use of equalsIgnoreCase in HTTP parameter processing logic. Monitor for unexpected process execution or file changes on the server following web requests with suspicious parameters.
